findings.title: Attack time is calculated but NEVER used in classification
findings.impact: HIGH - Fast vs slow attack is key to drum classification but completely ignored

findings.title: Rigid frequency band thresholds cause misclassification
findings.evidence: if (frequency < 250.0f) return DrumBand::Kick; else if (frequency < 800.0f) return DrumBand::Snare;
findings.impact: HIGH - Real kicks can have dominant freq at 300-400Hz, real snares can peak at 4000Hz+

findings.title: Single FFT peak misses perceptually important frequencies
findings.evidence: Finds maxMag and returns single peakIndex frequency
findings.impact: MEDIUM - A kick's click transient can overshadow its body, causing wrong classification

findings.title: classifySubType only uses band, flatness, dominantFreq
findings.evidence: DrumSubType classifySubType(DrumBand band, float spectralFlatness, float dominantFreq)
findings.impact: HIGH - attackTimeMs is available in result but not passed to classification function

findings.title: Color-to-category mapping in SampleBrowserPage is CORRECT
findings.evidence: colorToCategory lambda correctly maps all 21 DrumColors to DrumCategory
findings.impact: N/A - This is working correctly, problem is upstream

root_cause: DrumAnalyzer assigns wrong DrumSubType (and thus wrong color) because classification relies only on rigid frequency thresholds and spectral flatness. Attack time is calculated but never used, and dominant frequency analysis doesn't account for transient vs body distinction.
